correctness.rationale: The stated coordinate inequalities are equivalent to Minkowski addition of (ell-a)/2 times the coordinate cube and a/2 times the diagonal segment: coordinate range <=ell-a and absolute coordinate bounds ensure an admissible common shift. The support function is half(ell-a)sum|g_i|+half(a)|sum g_i|. For almost every Gaussian normal g, signs of coordinates and sign of total specify exactly 2^(d+1)-2 distinct vertices; impossible are two opposite total-sign sign-vectors. The half-normal comparison yields q_dj and 2 binom(d,j) for each 1<=j<=d, and coupling a positive half-normal increase proves strict levels. Signed half-normal Berry-Esseen has identical variance and bounded third moment uniformly in j, giving c=sqrt(2/(pi-2)). The central limit of (sum signs,sum G) with correlation sqrt(2/pi), conditioned on sum G positive, gives the asserted skew-normal density; 2D/3D orthant identities provide arcsine exact moments. Independently sampled 100,000 Gaussian normal directions in each d=2,3,5,16; compared rank mean/variance to exact formulas, checked 2^-d weighted sum of half-normal q values ~1 (within 0.004 for d=2 and tighter later), and checked d=2 exact angles. These are finite confirmations, not replacements for the general probability proof.
